_comment: Catalog of conda channels IDOL knows about. Separate from the ACTIVE list, which lives in each project's environment.yml — adding to this catalog is free, adding to the active list costs a repodata fetch on every solve. `tier` is mainstream | domain | vendor. `conflicts_with` drives the mixed-channel warning; `requires_order_below` names channels that must be searched BEFORE this one.

channels.description: Community-led alternative to defaults. The largest channel, often with more up-to-date package versions and an entirely open-source ecosystem.
channels.notes: IDOL's recommended default. Miniforge ships conda-forge-only out of the box.

channels.description: Anaconda's own curated channels, maintained by Anaconda Inc. Expands to pkgs/main, pkgs/r, and on Windows pkgs/msys2. Packages are built against Anaconda's compiler and BLAS stack.
channels.notes: Anaconda's Terms of Service require a paid Business plan for organisations with 200+ employees or contractors to use Anaconda-maintained channels. Community channels on anaconda.org (conda-forge, bioconda) are exempt. Government entities and large nonprofits/academia are not blanket-exempt. Removing this channel writes `nodefaults` into environment.yml.

channels.description: Dedicated to bioinformatics software — genomics tools, RNA/DNA workflows, biological data analysis.
channels.notes: Linux and macOS only; Windows is not supported. Bioconda dropped defaults from its recommended channel set in August 2024.

channels.description: Official PyTorch builds — torch, torchvision, torchaudio, and the CUDA-enabled variants.
channels.notes: GPU builds usually need the nvidia channel searched alongside this one. Nightly builds live under the label channel `pytorch/label/nightly`.

channels.description: NVIDIA's CUDA toolkit, cuDNN, and GPU runtime libraries packaged for conda.
channels.notes: Only useful on machines with an NVIDIA GPU. Adds a substantial repodata fetch.

channels.description: Intel-optimised builds of Python and numerical libraries, built against Intel's MKL and compilers for x86 performance.
channels.notes: Mixing these builds with conda-forge's can produce ABI mismatches; prefer one numerical stack per environment.

channels.description: NVIDIA RAPIDS — GPU-accelerated dataframe and machine-learning libraries (cuDF, cuML, cuGraph) with pandas- and scikit-learn-like APIs.
channels.notes: Linux only, and requires a supported NVIDIA GPU. Needs the nvidia channel for its CUDA dependencies.
